chapter.title: Logs & Evidence
chapter.sub: The lobby processor changed overnight. Three logs, three times — and the answer mustn’t be destroyed finding it.
chapter.status: **DRAFT** · scripted from the series plan · IDs provisional

items.text: SEASON 9 · EPISODE 6 · DRAFT  The security office · Maya, Raffa, Solveig and Dario · Level L5 · Advanced support (formulas on request)  The lobby processor changed overnight. Three logs say three different times. Before anyone fixes anything, somebody has to find out what happened — without destroying the answer.  ⚑ RV-170: security owns evidence; the network and time server are Raffa’s. RV-175: logs contain people. RV-172: figures illustrative. Some choices run on a clock.

items.title: Logs & Evidence
items.stakes: Someone changed the lobby processor overnight. Three logs disagree about when — and the wall opens in nine hours.
items.reward: One timeline, one clock, and the evidence intact.

Log in to the processor and look around

items.title: Three clocks.
items.body: Raffa reads the sources. The switch logs in UTC. The jump host logs in local time — UTC−5. And the processor has had no time server since handover: its NTP address points at the integrator's commissioning laptop, long gone, so it has kept its own time — 11 minutes 25 seconds slow after 120 days. Converted to UTC, 01:58:40, 02:10:05 and 07:10:02 are the same moment.
items.label: Test: the local time — and the drift in ppm.

items.sub: Advanced · the skill behind this chapter

items.alt: A teaching moment: Maya and Raffa beside a board. The switch says 07:10 UTC. The jump host says 02:10 local. The processor says 01:58. UTC minus five makes the switch 02:10 too. The processor is eleven minutes and twenty-five seconds slow — no time server since handover. About sixty-six parts per million over four months. Timeline in UTC, then Solveig decides what happens next.

items.caption: Advanced: the formula is there if you ask. Try without it first.

items.text: 📙 ON REQUEST · ADVANCED  Terms   Audit log   Chain of custody   NTP   If you need it   ƒ Ask for the formula · Local time from UTC   ƒ FORMULA · Local time from UTC  t local  = t UTC  + offset   t UTC   the time in Coordinated Universal Time  offset  the zone's offset from UTC, hours (negative west of Greenwich)  t local   local clock time — add or subtract 24 h, and change the date, if it crosses midnight      ƒ Ask for the formula · Clock drift   ƒ FORMULA · Clock drift  drift = ppm × 10 −6  × t   ppm  frequency error, parts per million  t  elapsed time, s  drift  time error, s

items.text: Act II — “An approved session that did more”

items.title: An approved session that did more.
items.body: The UTC timeline tells a small, ordinary story. At 07:05 UTC one of Dario's named technicians opened an approved jump-host session — signage-player firmware, 01:30 to 03:00 local. At 07:10 UTC he changed the lobby processor's default input to test a player, and forgot to change it back. No break-in. An approval that said when, but never said what.
items.label: Test: when in the window — and what the approval lacked.

known: ◉ NTP pointed at a missing laptop
items.risk: The next investigation with three clocks.
timeout: The DSPs are still on their own clocks.

hints.text: Who should own the building's time?

options.label: Set the processor's clock by hand
options.result: In four months it's minutes out again.

options.label: Ask Raffa to point every AV device at his time server, write timelines in UTC, and check every device's offset on his dashboard each month
options.result: By noon every device is within 50 ms of the time server.
options.consequence: One source of time, owned by the network's owner.

options.label: Point them all at the integrator's new laptop
options.consequence: A time source that leaves when the integrator does.

options.label: Don't bother — the order of events is enough
options.result: Order across three devices needs one clock.
options.consequence: Can't order what you can't align.

items.title: The day of two noons
items.body: Until 1883 most North American towns kept their own local time, set by the sun, and the railways juggled dozens of them. On 18 November 1883 the railways switched to a handful of standard time zones; some towns saw noon twice that day as their clocks were set back. Timetables — and the records of what happened when — finally agreed on what time it was.

items.text: ✦ UX RULE #87 · AVERY'S LENS  One clock for every log  A timeline is only as good as its clocks. Every device should take time from the same source, and every timeline should be written in UTC.  Three logs said 01:58, 02:10 and 07:10. They were the same moment — on three different clocks.

items.alt: The log sheet as one UTC timeline: 07:05 jump-host session opens, named technician, scope players; 07:10:02 the processor's input changes, outside scope, highlighted; 07:10:02 the switch sees the session; 12:40 the input restored under change 2231; now every AV device within 50 ms of the time server.
items.caption: One moment. One clock.

items.title: NTP: 10.40.0.201
items.body: The lobby processor's time settings: ‘NTP server 10.40.0.201’. Raffa checks: .201 was the integrator's commissioning laptop, gone since handover. The processor has kept its own time — badly — for four months.

items.alt: The lobby at 17:30; the wall shows its normal content; Solveig holds a sealed evidence folder; Maya beside her.

bubbles.text: Evidence kept, timeline in UTC, a gap closed. And the wall's on time.
Every clock in the building agrees with Raffa's now.

items.prompt: My tech feels terrible. He had an approved session. Is he in trouble?

options.label: “He had approval for when, not for what. That's our gap to close. Help us write scopes he can follow.”
options.reply: He'll write the first one himself. Players only, nothing else.

options.label: “He should have known better.”
options.reply: He should. So should whoever approved a session with no scope.

items.title: 01:30–03:00 · player firmware
items.body: Security's approval for the night: ‘Named tech, signage-player firmware, 01:30–03:00.’ No line for what the session may not touch. The jump host recorded it all.

items.alt: The MER; Raffa points at a switch whose ports are all one colour; Solveig holds an audit letter; Maya listens.

bubbles.text: The auditors want signage unable to reach control, and control unable to reach the guests. By the gala.
How much of it is flat now?

items.text: FIELD NOTE —  Evidence first: touch nothing, and let security export logs and configuration read-only and record who handled them. Note every log’s time source, convert to UTC (t_local = t_UTC + offset) and measure the drift (ppm × 10⁻⁶ × t). Put every device on the network owner’s time server. Approve sessions for a written scope, not just a window — then restore the service through change control.
REFLECTION (optional)  · If something changed in your systems last night, whose clock would you believe?
